title: Minimal private stack contract and interactive upgrade playbook
creator: Priya Patel
description: Context: Customers operating in fully isolated VPCs and air-gapped on-prem sites require a minimal, auditable contract that defines the networking and artifact constraints we guarantee during bootstrap and routine upgrades. This ticket captures a concise product contract (what we promise) and an operational playbook for interactive upgrades when offline constraints prevent fully automated operator flows.
scope_in:
- Minimal networking contract for bootstrap and upgrades (minimal outbound endpoints, allowlist semantics, optional proxy).
- Interactive upgrade playbook for operator-driven upgrades in constrained networks.
- Acceptance checks and test harness to validate offline artifact integrity and operator rollback.
- Clear upgrade-time SLAs and manual rollback triggers.
- Documentation and runbook links for customers and SREs.
scope_out:
- Full implementation of a zero-touch operatorless bootstrap (separate epic).
- Support for highly-customized OS-level firewalls; we provide guidance but not host-specific scripts.
- Automated long-running mirror infrastructure (we will reference partner solutions).
requirements: Network: Define minimal outbound allowlist set (FQDNs and IP ranges) required for optional mirrored bootstrap and image provenance checks.
Artifacts: Must support signed artifact manifests (SHA256 + optional secondary hash) and allow customers to provide an airgap bundle (tarball) with signature verification.
Bootstrap: Operator must be able to perform an interactive bootstrap when only ephemeral egress is permitted (short windows) using tokenized ephemeral fetch flows.
Upgrade: Provide a staged interactive upgrade flow: precheck -> snapshot -> apply on canary subset -> validation window -> full rollout or rollback.
Observability: Upgrade run must emit telemetry (success/fail, latency, artifact hash) to the customer-visible console and an optional offline log bundle export.
Security: KMS rotation and key provenance checks must be supported during upgrade and must not require outbound egress after initial manifest verification.
Operator UX: Console must expose an interactive control to ‘stage and hold’ an upgrade at each step and surface detailed failure diagnostics and remediation hints.
Fallbacks: When artifact verification is impossible (manifest missing or hash mismatch), operator must be required to approve forced rollback and an audit log generated.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Minimal allowlist documented and validated by automated connectivity test that runs in an isolated test VPC. Test report includes deterministic success/failure codes and a human-readable checklist.
AC-2: Airgap bundle ingestion: customer can upload a signed artifact tarball; system verifies signatures and computes SHA256, producing a verification report that can be exported.
AC-3: Interactive upgrade flow executed in a staging cluster with no persistent egress; canary nodes upgraded and validated by automated smoke tests within a configurable validation window.
AC-4: Rollback path: Induced failure during canary must trigger documented rollback that restores previous runtime images and KV cache consistency within SLA (defined below).

AC-5: Telemetry and audit: Every interactive upgrade step must append an entry to the audit log with operator identity, timestamp, artifact hash, and step outcome; logs must be exportable as a signed bundle.
AC-6: Security review: Design passes internal security checklist including KMS integration and proof that key material is not exfiltrated during interactive flows (security_review_required = true).

AC-7: Operator console: UI shows explicit blocking gates for artifact mismatches, network timeouts, and validation failures; gating leads to a clearly labeled ‘force proceed’ with confirmation and reason required.
rollout_plan:
1) Draft minimal contract doc and runbook -> internal review.
2) Implement connectivity test harness and artifact verifier in staging.
3) Run two dry upgrades in an isolated lab (one mirror-based, one upload-based).
4) Capture telemetry and update console UI to add staging hold points.
5) Publish runbook and onboarding checklist for initial pilot customers.
6) Pilot with 2 customers for 8 weeks, gather issues, iterate.
Fallback: If verification fails consistently, pause rollout and open ENG follow-up tickets.
test_plan: TP-1: Connectivity harness that simulates constrained egress (allowlist only) and validates DNS resolution, TLS handshake, and proxy pass-through with deterministic results.
TP-2: Airgap bundle CI: create signed tar, corrupt a byte, ensure verification fails and audit captures operator intervention.
TP-3: Upgrade canary test: upgrade 3-node canary, run smoke tests (model inference, slot allocation, KV cache hit rate), measure recovery time on rollback.
TP-4: Latency and SLA validation: measure time from 'start upgrade' to 'canary validation complete' under network constraints for baseline SLA.
TP-5: User acceptance: runbook walkthrough with customer SRE, capture feedback and required clarifications.
monitoring_and_sla: SLA-1: For interactive upgrades we commit to a canary validation window of X minutes (configurable); default 15 minutes. If rollback is triggered, aim to restore prior state within 30 minutes for clusters <= 50 nodes.
SLA-2: Telemetry latency: audit logs must be available in the console within 60 seconds of each step completion when egress is available; when offline they must be exportable on request.
M-1: Key metrics to surface: artifact_verification_status, canary_success_rate, rollback_incidents, operator_forced_proceeds.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Customer firewall blocks required endpoints unexpectedly -> Mitigation: Provide diagnostic connectivity harness and a single-run 'ephemeral fetch' token flow to scope a small outbound window.
Risk: Corrupt or tampered airgap bundle -> Mitigation: Strict signature checks, multi-hash validation, human operator gate with explicit audit entry before force proceed.
Risk: Upgrade leaves model serving in degraded state because KV cache inconsistent -> Mitigation: Snapshot KV cache pre-upgrade and verify post-rollback restore path in tests.
Risk: Operator confusion over interactive steps -> Mitigation: UI copy changes, inline runbook snippets, pre-filled remediation commands, mandatory confirmation with short rationale.
comments: 2025-02-18 Priya Patel: Created ticket to capture minimal contract + interactive upgrade playbook. Initial ask from sales (customer ACME) for clear upgrade SLAs and offline artifact verification.
2025-02-20 Diego Morales: Engineering notes - verifier prototype exists but needs multi-hash support; will add SHA256+SHA512. Estimate 6 dev days for core flows.
2025-02-25 Ava Chen (Security): Flagged KMS rotation during offline upgrades. We need to prove no key material leaves the site. Recommend HSM integration doc be referenced.
2025-03-01 Liam O'Sullivan: Runtime constraint: KV cache snapshot/restore must be part of canary precheck to avoid degraded serving post-upgrade. Adding test cases to harness.
2025-03-05 Priya Patel: Updated acceptance criteria to add explicit audit-export requirement after review with compliance. Set status to Planned and assigned to Diego for kickoff.
decisions: D-1: Use signed artifact manifests (SHA256 canonical) as the minimum verification requirement for airgap bundles.
D-2: Interactive upgrade will default to a canary subset (5% or minimum 3 nodes) and require explicit hold before full rollout.
D-3: Security review required and must sign off on KMS/HSM interactions before pilot.
